stories.h: Record US cyclospora outbreak ends after nearly 13,000 linked cases
stories.w: The FDA says recalled iceberg lettuce is now off the market, but investigators still do not know how contamination spread widely enough to drive the largest outbreak recorded in the country.

stories.h: Canada holds back from another round of trade retaliation
stories.w: Prime Minister Mark Carney described Washington's newest restrictions as relatively modest and signalled restraint, easing the immediate risk of further escalation between the deeply integrated economies.

stories.h: Brazil's Supreme Court crisis spills into the election campaign
stories.w: The court cancelled a second consecutive session amid allegations involving justices, police and a failed bank, an extraordinary institutional rupture weeks before national elections.

stories.h: US terrorist list for Latin American criminal groups grows to 21
stories.w: The latest designation of Ecuador's Los Tiguerones expands a framework Washington has used to justify joint operations and lethal strikes against organizations traditionally treated as criminal gangs.

stories.h: Russia and Ukraine intensify long-range attacks on cities and energy sites
stories.w: Russian strikes killed five people near shopping centres and wounded dozens, while Ukraine launched a 777-drone barrage that hit Russian logistics and refining targets, according to officials on both sides.

stories.h: Sweden approaches an election that could put the far right in cabinet
stories.w: More than eight million voters choose between rival blocs on Sunday, with the Sweden Democrats positioned to enter government for the first time if the right retains power.

stories.h: Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak reaches a seventh province
stories.w: A laboratory-confirmed case appeared in South-Ubangi after the patient travelled across several provinces; 38 contacts are quarantined as the national toll reaches 3,349 deaths.

stories.h: Nigeria suspends parliamentary visits to South Africa over anti-migrant violence
stories.w: The National Assembly halted official engagements indefinitely after attacks forced thousands of African migrants from South Africa and sharpened diplomatic tensions across the continent.

stories.h: BRICS leaders meet as wars and rivalry test the expanded bloc
stories.w: Leaders representing 11 countries and roughly half the world's population gathered in New Delhi to discuss trade, energy, supply chains and alternatives to Western-dominated financial systems.

stories.h: Hong Kong jails two Tiananmen vigil leaders for seven years
stories.w: Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung were sentenced for inciting subversion, extending the national-security crackdown that ended the city's once-legal public commemorations of 1989.

stories.h: Indonesia's wildfire-related respiratory cases more than double in eight days
stories.w: Health ministry figures rose from 50,891 to 113,336 as haze exposed more than 12.5 million people across seven provinces during the country's worst fire season in 11 years.

stories.h: Queensland loses a credit-rating notch as infrastructure debt rises
stories.w: S&P cut the state's long-term rating from AA+ to AA, citing weak budgets and structurally higher debt as major spending accelerates before the 2032 Brisbane Olympics.

stories.h: Varroa mite makes a 1,000-kilometre jump into Far North Queensland
stories.w: Biosecurity officials confirmed Australia's northernmost detections of the destructive bee parasite and suspect human-assisted hive movement, raising risks for pollination-dependent agriculture.
